questions.explanation: For predictions based on present evidence, use 'be going to'.
questions.q: Look at those clouds! It ___ rain.

questions.explanation: For instant decisions and offers, use 'will'.
questions.q: I ___ help you with your bags.

questions.explanation: For plans decided before speaking, use 'be going to'.
questions.q: She ___ a doctor. She decided it last year.

questions.explanation: A prediction based on what you see now uses 'be going to'.
questions.q: Watch out! You ___ drop your phone!

questions.explanation: Predictions with 'I think' about the future often use 'will'.
questions.q: I think it ___ sunny tomorrow.

questions.explanation: A fixed plan uses 'be going to'.
questions.q: We ___ visit our grandparents this weekend. We bought the tickets.

questions.explanation: An offer decided at the moment of speaking uses 'will'.
questions.q: A: I'm thirsty. B: I ___ get you some water.

questions.explanation: Promises use 'will' ('won't' in the negative).
questions.q: I promise I ___ late again.

questions.explanation: A decision made before speaking uses 'be going to'.
questions.q: We've decided: we ___ to Spain in June.

questions.explanation: A decision made at the moment of speaking uses 'will'.
questions.q: A: The room is cold. B: I ___ close the window.

questions.explanation: After 'will' use the base verb: 'will help'.
questions.q: Which sentence is correct?

questions.explanation: Predictions based on present evidence use 'be going to'.
questions.q: Look! That car ___ crash!

questions.explanation: A plan made earlier uses 'be going to'.
questions.q: I ___ my homework tonight. I planned it this morning.

questions.explanation: An instant decision uses 'will'.
questions.q: A: I forgot my wallet. B: Don't worry, I ___ pay.

questions.explanation: After 'will' use the base verb, not 'to': 'will call'.
options: We are going to travel in July.
He will to call you tonight.
questions.q: Which sentence has a mistake?

questions.explanation: A future event based on present evidence uses 'be going to'.
questions.q: She's pregnant. She ___ a baby in May.

questions.explanation: General predictions about the distant future often use 'will'.
questions.q: In my opinion, robots ___ do all the work one day.

questions.explanation: 'Going to' expresses a plan decided before now.
questions.q: I'm ___ study hard this year. I decided in September.

questions.explanation: An offer decided now uses 'will'.
questions.q: A: Can you carry this? B: Sure, I ___.

questions.explanation: A prediction based on what you see uses 'be going to'.
questions.q: The sky is dark. It ___ snow.
